title: E2E: POST article with DID sig, verify X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Verified
description:
What: End-to-end test: submit an article with a valid X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Sig header over raw TCP NNTP, then retrieve via ARTICLE and check X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Verified: true is present.

Algorithm:
1. Add test in crates/integration-tests/tests/ or crates/reader/tests/
2. Setup: spin up in-process reader server with ServerStores::new_mem() on a random port (same pattern as nntp_conformance.rs)
3. Generate Ed25519 key pair using ed25519_dalek in the test
4. Compute did:key URL for the public key (encode as did:key:z<base58btc(multicodec_prefix + pub_bytes)>)
5. Build article bytes: standard headers + body
6. Sign article bytes with private key -> 64-byte sig -> base64url-no-pad
7. Construct header value: format!('{}  {}', did_key_url, sig_b64) — note: test must use the exact format parse_did_sig expects
8. Build full article with X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Sig header injected before the blank line
9. POST article via TCP (same helpers as nntp_conformance.rs: write_all, read_line)
10. Wait for 240 response
11. Send ARTICLE <msgid>
12. Read full response including headers
13. Assert response starts with 220
14. Assert response headers contain 'X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Verified: true'
15. Also test with wrong signature: POST similar article with mangled sig, ARTICLE it, assert 'X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Verified: false'

Defensive programming:
- Test article must have unique Message-ID per run (include timestamp or random)
- Close TCP connections cleanly
- Use tokio::time::timeout to prevent hangs
